summary: Wallabies coach Eddie Jones again denied contact with Japan and said he is '100 percent' committed to coaching Australia through to the 2027 World Cup, though he conceded the decision is not his alone and a formal independent review is coming. He defended his choice of youth over experienced players after Australia became the first Australian side to exit a Rugby World Cup in the pool stages. Jones argued the problems lie in the wider development system and that Australia can reach the top level by 2027.
one_line: Eddie Jones denies Japan talks and says he is committed to coaching the Wallabies to 2027 despite a World Cup pool-stage exit and a pending review.
key_facts: Eddie Jones said at a Tuesday media conference that he is '100 percent' passionate about continuing to coach the Wallabies and said 'I'm staying.'

Jones said staying through the next World Cup is 'the intention' but that the coach doesn't decide how long he stays; on seeing out his contract to the end of 2027 he said 'It's not absolutely my decision.'
Jones refused to answer a question on potential break clauses in his contract with Rugby Australia.
Rugby Australia has said it intends to back Jones, and he said he believed he had official support.
A formal review of the World Cup campaign will be done by independent consultants, and Jones said he was ready to participate; the team and coaches had already completed their own review.

Jones was named Wallabies coach at the start of 2023 as replacement for Dave Rennie, promising the Rugby Championship, Bledisloe Cup and a 'smash and grab' on the World Cup, none of which were achieved.
The Wallabies became the first Australian team to bow out of a Rugby World Cup in the pool stages.
Jones finished the year with a 2-7 win-loss record, with the only two wins coming against Georgia and Portugal.
Jones said he had no regrets leaving experienced players such as Quade Cooper and Michael Hooper out of the World Cup squad, saying he chose to 'go with youth.'
Jones again denied reports that he interviewed for the Japan head coach role, saying 'I haven't been speaking to anyone, mate.'
Australia, a two-time world champion, is currently ranked 10th in the world.
Jones said Australia is 'not at that level' of the quarterfinalists but can be by 2027, and that the development system underneath the national team needs fixing.
